High Court Of Judicature At Allahabad

sentences.text:
?Neutral Citation No. - 2024:Ahc:175888
Court No. - 66

Case :- Criminal Misc. Bail Application No. - 40931 of 2024
Applicant :- Hanifa

Opposite Party :- State of U.P.
Counsel for Applicant :- Javed Raza

Counsel for Opposite Party :- G.A.
Hon'ble Sameer Jain,J.
1.

Heard Sri Ramesh Chandra Yadav, Advocate holding brief of Sri Javed Raza, learned counsel for the applicant and Dr. S.B. Maurya, learned AGA-I, for the State.
2. The instant application has been filed seeking release of the applicant on bail in Case Crime No.
0290 of 2024, under Sections 498A and 304B IPC and 3/4 DP Act, Police Station Baheri, District Bareilly, during pendency of the trial in the court below.

3. Learned counsel for the applicant submitted that applicant is mother in law of the deceased and on the basis of false allegation of demand of dowry and torture she has been made accused in the present case alongwith her family members.

4. He next submitted that applicant resided in District Udham Singh Nagar, Uttarakhand while deceased resided along with her husband in District Bareilly, Uttar Pradesh and this fact is evident from the voter identity card of applicant which has been annexed at page no. 32 of the paper book and as applicant is resided separately, therefore, she was not having any concern with the family Hanifa vs State Of U.P. on 8 November, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/85413273/
1 affairs of the deceased and it appears that some dispute arose between husband and wife and thereafter wife consumed some poisonous substance and died.

5. He further submitted that during post-mortem, however, cause of death could not be ascertained and viscera was preserved but from viscera report it reflects that due to consumption of insecticide,
deceased died and viscera report is now on record which has been annexed at page no. 52 of the paper book which shows that deceased died due to consumption of insecticide, therefore, viscera report also suggest that it is a case of suicidal death.

6. He further submits that applicant is a lady and there is no specific allegation against her and she is having no criminal history and in the present matter, she is in jail since 12.06.2024 i.e., for the last more than four months.

7. Per contra, learned AGA opposed the prayer for bail and submitted that applicant is mother-in-law of the deceased and she died within two years of her marriage under abnormal circumstances and there is also demand of dowry but could not dispute the fact that there is no specific allegation against applicant and applicant resided separately from deceased.
8. Learned AGA further could not dispute the fact that from the viscera report, it reflects that deceased died due to consumption of insecticide.

9. I have heard learned counsel for the parties and perused the record of the case.
10.

However, daughter in law of applicant died within two years of her marriage under abnormal circumstances and there is also allegation of demand of dowry but applicant is mother in law of deceased and there is no specific allegation against her.

11. Further, from the record it also reflects that applicant resided separately from deceased and viscera report suggest that deceased died due to consumption of insecticide and therefore, at this stage, it cannot be said that it is not a case of suicidal death.
12. Further, applicant is a lady and she is having no criminal history and in the present matter, she is in jail since 12.06.2024.

13. Therefore, considering the facts and circumstances of the case, discussed above, in my view,
applicant is entitled to be released on bail.
14. Accordingly, without expressing any opinion on the merits of the case, the instant bail application is allowed.

15. Let the applicant-Hanifa, be released on bail in the aforesaid case on furnishing a personal bond and two sureties each in the like amount to the satisfaction of the court concerned with the following conditions:-
Hanifa vs State Of U.P. on 8 November, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/85413273/
2
( i ) The applicant shall appear before the trial court on the dates fixed, unless her personal presence is exempted.

(ii) The applicant shall not directly or indirectly, make inducement, threat or promise to any person acquainted with the facts of the case so as to dissuade her from disclosing such facts to the Court or any police officer or tamper with the evidence.
(iii) The applicant shall not indulge in any criminal and anti-social activity.
16. In case of breach of any of the above condition, the prosecution will be at liberty to move an application before this Court for cancellation of the bail of the applicant.

17. It is clarified that the observations made herein are limited to the facts brought in by the parties pertaining to the disposal of bail application and the said observations shall have no bearing on the merits of the case during trial.
Order Date :- 8.11.2024 #Vik/-
